storyTitle: Croydon Youth Justice Plan lacks detailed Stop and Search data for children
headline: Croydon challenges missing child stop and search figures
committee: Scrutiny Children & Young People Sub-Committee Croydon, 20 October 2026
keyPointsHeading: What did the scrutiny review reveal?

watchability.hook: Croydon challenges missing child stop and search figures
watchability.hookStyle: Immediate factual council decision and resident impact
watchability.localRelevance: Directly affects Croydon residents and council services

claims.statement: Child stop and searches in Croydon increased by thirty-six per cent to 1,262 incidents.
claims.sourceQuote: The plan acknowledges an increase in stop and searches of children by 36%, rising from approximately 930 to 1,262 incidents.
claims.sourceDocument: Scrutiny Children & Young People Sub-Committee Croydon, 20 October 2026

claims.statement: Councillors highlighted the absence of data detailing ethnicity, age, and outcomes for child searches.
claims.sourceQuote: Councillor Daoud asked if the board could share the figures by ethnicity, age, and outcome, arrest, charge, or no further action. Mr Collins responded that that information is held by the police.
claims.sourceDocument: Scrutiny Children & Young People Sub-Committee Croydon, 20 October 2026

claims.statement: Only two children were on remand, reflecting lower custody usage across the borough.
claims.sourceQuote: The Youth Justice Plan outlines progress in reducing the use of custody, with only two children currently on remand.
claims.sourceDocument: Scrutiny Children & Young People Sub-Committee Croydon, 20 October 2026

takeawayCard.title: Councillors demand complete racial data
takeawayCard.subtitle: Officers promise ongoing discussions over stark ethnic disproportionality.

keyPoints: Child stop and search incidents rose thirty-six per cent across Croydon.
The plan lacked detailed data on ethnic background, age, and outcomes.
Only two children are currently held on remand across the borough.
